source: Wikipedia: Spreading activation
finding: Spreading activation searches a network. Source nodes get weights. The weights spread to linked nodes and usually decay with each step. Discrete weights are called marker passing. It was invented in cognitive psychology and later applied to information retrieval over document and term networks.
numbers: No numbers.
quote: Spreading activation is a method for searching associative networks, biological and artificial neural networks, or semantic networks.
limits: Encyclopedia page, secondary. Its algorithm section is flagged as written like a research paper.
agent_relevance: Gives the minimal algorithm for S3 retrieval: seed, spread, decay, threshold, read out top nodes.

source: Wikipedia: Spreading activation (priming example)
finding: The theory explains semantic priming: a word is recognised faster after a related prime than after an unrelated one. Example: doctor after nurse versus after carrot. Closer meaning is drawn as a shorter link, so activation arrives sooner.
numbers: No numbers.
limits: Textbook example only.
agent_relevance: A cue should lift its neighbours, not only exact matches.

source: Wikipedia: Priming (psychology)
finding: Semantic priming is credited to Meyer and Schvaneveldt (1971), Facilitation in recognizing pairs of words, J Exp Psychol 90(2):227-234. The page notes that behavioural (social) priming was hit by the 2012 replication crisis, while Meyer (2014, Science) wrote that semantic priming is well established.
numbers: No effect sizes on the page.
limits: Do not mix social priming failures with word-level semantic priming. The word-level effect has large datasets (see a13).
agent_relevance: Replication failure of social priming does not undermine lexical priming; keep evidence tags separate.

source: Collins and Loftus (1975) A spreading-activation theory of semantic processing, Psychological Review 82(6):407-428
finding: Theory as described by secondary sources (SpreadPy, Lucas 2000, Hutchison 2003): concepts are nodes. Link length shows relatedness. Activation spreads outward, weakens with distance and time, and must pass a threshold to be used. It builds on Quillian's model. It keeps a lexical network and a separate semantic network.
numbers: Not read. Full text is paywalled and every mirror I tried returned HTML or a 403.
limits: Details come from secondary papers, not from the paper itself.
agent_relevance: The founding spec for S3: activation, decay with distance, threshold, link strength = relatedness.

source: Collins and Quillian (1969) Retrieval time from semantic memory, J Verbal Learn Verbal Behav 8:240-247
finding: Origin of the hierarchical network model: facts stored at the highest node where they apply. Lucas (2000) cites it for the hierarchical category view of concepts.
numbers: Not read. ScienceDirect blocked the request.
limits: Exact reaction times not verified. Later critiques of strict hierarchy are from general knowledge, not checked this session.
agent_relevance: A free weighted graph is more flexible than a strict hierarchy for agent facts.

source: Meyer and Schvaneveldt (1971) Facilitation in recognizing pairs of words, J Exp Psychol 90(2):227-234
finding: First lexical-decision priming result: related pairs (such as bread-butter) are judged faster than unrelated pairs. Hutchison (2003) and Lucas (2000) note that these earliest pairs came from association norms, so the effect was associative priming.
numbers: Not read. No ms values verified.
limits: Pairs were associates, so association and meaning overlap are confounded.
agent_relevance: A cue lowers the cost of reaching a related item. Cheap to measure.

source: Neely (1977) Semantic priming and retrieval from lexical memory: roles of inhibitionless spreading activation and limited-capacity attention, J Exp Psychol Gen 106(3):226-254
finding: Two processes: fast automatic spreading activation without inhibition, and a slower limited-capacity attention process that follows expectancy. SOA is used to separate them. Secondary sources say attention cannot act under about 250 ms SOA.
numbers: Not read. The scispace and typeset PDFs returned an HTML shell. No ms numbers verified.
limits: Secondary descriptions only (a web search summary, Hutchison 2003, Lucas 2000).
agent_relevance: Two routes match our agent: cheap automatic expansion first, costly controlled search only on a signal (G1).

source: Hutchison (2003) Is semantic priming due to association strength or feature overlap? A microanalytic review, Psychon Bull Rev 10(4):785-813
finding: Early work read priming as automatic spreading activation along associative links (Anderson 1983; Collins and Loftus 1975; Neely 1977; Posner and Snyder 1975). Automatic means quick and unintended. Two strategies inflate lexical-decision priming: expectancy (long SOA) and semantic matching (high nonword ratio).
numbers: Review of many studies; no single N.
quote: there is no universal SOA that distinctly separates conscious from unconscious processing
limits: There is no universal SOA that separates automatic from conscious processing, and it varies by task.
agent_relevance: When we test retrieval, avoid designs where the gain could come from strategy and not from the graph.

source: Hutchison (2003) mediated priming section
finding: Spreading activation predicts priming across two links (lion to stripes via tiger). De Groot (1983) found priming only for direct associates in seven experiments, a failure for multi-link spread. Later studies found mediated priming when lists held only mediated and unrelated items, which cuts strategy.
numbers: Table 2, standard lexical decision, unrelated baseline: de Groot Exp 1 direct 43 ms, mediated 19 ms. Neutral baseline: direct 26 ms, mediated 2 ms (n.s.).
limits: The PDF table text is garbled, read with care. Mediated effects are small. Chwilla et al. (2000) disagreed.
agent_relevance: Activation two hops away is weak. Expect fast decay past one or two hops and do not rely on long chains.

source: Hutchison (2003) conclusions
finding: Automatic priming appears to come from both association strength and feature overlap. Mediated associates support associative priming. Functional associates, synonyms and antonyms support feature overlap. Category coordinates and perceptually similar items did not prime automatically in the visual modality.
numbers: Review-level claim, no single effect size.
limits: Disputes Lucas (2000), who found pure semantic priming without association.
agent_relevance: Keep both association edges and similarity edges in the memory graph.

source: Lucas (2000) Semantic priming without association: a meta-analytic review, Psychon Bull Rev 7(4):618-630
finding: Automatic semantic priming exists without association. Average semantic priming was about half of associative priming, an associative boost. Priming did not vary much with prime time, relatedness proportion or task, except naming gave smaller effects.
numbers: 26 studies, 116 semantic observations, mean d = .26 (by study .30). Associative: 73 observations, d = .51 (by study .49, 20 studies). 3,882 subjects counting repeats, 2,243 after correction. Power .80 needs N = 188 for semantic versus N = 72 for associative priming.
limits: Small effect. Hutchison (2003) disputes the pure-semantic conclusion for several relation types.
agent_relevance: Associated items give about twice the lift of merely similar items. Weight explicit links above embedding similarity when both exist.

source: Lucas (2000) task comparison
finding: Effect sizes by task were similar for lexical decision and semantic matching, and smaller for naming.
numbers: Lexical decision d = .27 (16 observations); semantic matching d = .26 (23 observations).
limits: Naming value not extracted reliably.
agent_relevance: Priming gain depends on the task. Test on the real downstream task, not a proxy (G7).

source: Hutchison et al. (2013) The Semantic Priming Project, Behav Res Methods 45:1099-1114
finding: Largest priming database: speeded naming and lexical decision for 1,661 targets after related or unrelated primes, at 200 and 1,200 ms SOA, from 768 subjects at four universities, plus attention and reading tests.
numbers: 1,661 targets, 768 subjects, 4 universities, 2 SOAs, 2 tasks, first-associate and other-associate primes.
limits: Provides data, not a test of one theory.
agent_relevance: Item-level ground truth to calibrate any activation model.

source: Hutchison et al. (2013) SPP: size of priming
finding: First-associate priming in lexical decision was about half of earlier estimates from a smaller regression study. Block order did not explain it.
numbers: SPP first associates: 26 ms (200 ms SOA), 20 ms (1,200 ms). Earlier study (Hutchison 2008): 42 and 60 ms. On 283 shared pairs: 43 and 61 ms before versus 25 and 23 ms in SPP. Block 1 vs 2: 19 and 18 ms (LDT), 6 and 6 ms (naming). Largest single item effect 262 ms.
limits: Shrinkage with a large varied sample. Small-sample priming results overstate.
agent_relevance: Expect real gains to be smaller than first demos. Plan for shrinkage when we test.

source: Hutchison et al. (2013) SPP: other associates and rank
finding: Associative rank may matter more than strength (Anaki and Henik 2003: no difference between FAS .10 and .42 if the item was the primary associate). Other-associate (2nd to nth response) priming can be absent or negative for single items.
numbers: Example item abandon at 200 ms SOA: first-associate priming 46.25 ms; other-associate priming -60.78 ms.
limits: Single-item values are noisy.
agent_relevance: Being a top-ranked neighbour matters more than raw link strength. Rank candidates; do not only threshold weights.

source: Citraro et al. (2025) SpreadPy, arXiv 2507.09628
finding: Python library for spreading activation on single-layer and multiplex networks. Parameters: retention R, diffusion strength Dx, and a threshold. Retention changes when activation peaks, not how high.
numbers: R = 0.2, 0.5, 0.8; Dx = 0.1, 1, 10. Raising R from 0.2 to 0.8 raised the easy-vs-hard timing effect from d = 0.37 to 0.61 while magnitude differences stayed about d = 0.78.
limits: Simulation study with no new participants. Effect sizes are between simulated conditions.
agent_relevance: Decay and threshold are separate dials: one sets speed, one sets reach. Tune them apart.

source: Citraro et al. (2025) SpreadPy: math anxiety case
finding: Activation seeded at mathematics reached anxiety faster and higher in networks of high-math-anxiety students than low-anxiety students. GPT-simulated students kept the rank order with weaker intensity.
numbers: Anxiety peak 15-25% higher in high-anxiety network at R = 0.2 to 0.8; peak above 35 units at R = 0.2; gap 5-6 units at R = 0.8. Probe stress gave peaks about two orders of magnitude smaller.
limits: Group sizes not captured in the text I read.
agent_relevance: Spread from a seed shows which associations dominate. It can expose bias in an agent's memory graph.

source: Citraro et al. (2025) SpreadPy: aphasia naming case
finding: Seeding the target word on a semantic plus phonological multiplex network gave activation timing that separated semantic from formal naming errors.
numbers: Multiplex of N = 4,118 word nodes (Small World of Words plus phonological edit distance). About 1,200 Philadelphia Naming Task trials, balanced across error types. Timing effect between error types up to d = 1.47 in the semantic layer at R = 0.8; some contrasts d about 1.94.
limits: Fitted to error classes, not compared with rival theories.
agent_relevance: Separate layers for meaning links and surface-form links is a clean design.

source: Citraro (2026) Early language learning via spreading activation and category exploration, arXiv 2607.06258
finding: Spreading activation on word-similarity graphs predicted the normative order of word learning in children better than a shortest-path baseline, in four languages, and matched the bursty category exploration in data.
numbers: Four languages (German, English, Dutch, Rioplatense Spanish), CDI norms; baselines: shortest path and 2,000 random permutations per language. Exact scores not extracted.
limits: Preprint; exact scores not read.
agent_relevance: Diffusion beats plain path distance for ordering related items.

source: Gutierrez et al. (2024) HippoRAG, arXiv 2405.14831
finding: An LLM builds a knowledge graph from the corpus. Query entities become seeds. Personalized PageRank (random walk with restarts, a close kin of spreading activation) ranks passages in one step.
numbers: Single-step average R@2/R@5: HippoRAG (ColBERTv2) 57.4/72.9 vs ColBERTv2 53.9/65.6. 2WikiMultiHopQA R@5 89.1 vs 68.2; MuSiQue R@5 51.9 vs 49.2; HotpotQA R@5 77.7 vs 79.3 (slightly worse). PPR damping 0.5, synonymy threshold 0.8. Claims 10-30x cheaper and 6-13x faster than IRCoT.
limits: PageRank is not decaying spread with a threshold. Gains largest on entity-heavy 2Wiki. Graph from OpenIE is noisy.
agent_relevance: Direct template for S3. Expect no gain, or a small loss, on simple single-hop sets.

source: Gutierrez et al. (2024) HippoRAG: all-recall and ablations
finding: Most gain comes from retrieving all needed passages. PPR beat simple ways to add associations. Adding only the direct neighbours of seeds without PPR scored worse.
numbers: All-recall top 5: gap to ColBERTv2 grows from 3 to 6 points on MuSiQue and from 20 to 38 on 2Wiki. PPR average R@5 72.9 versus roughly 56-59 for seed-only variants (approximate; table layout scrambled).
limits: Per-row ablation values uncertain because of table extraction.
agent_relevance: One-hop neighbour stuffing is not enough. Weighted multi-hop spread with restarts pays.

source: Pavlovic, Krasz and Hajdu (2026) SA-RAG: spreading activation for KG-based RAG, arXiv 2512.15922
finding: Spreading activation over an automatically built heterogeneous document graph retrieves evidence without LLM-guided graph walks. Works inside iterative pipelines with small open-weight models.
numbers: Up to 39% absolute gain in answer correctness over naive RAG when combined with chain-of-thought iterative retrieval. Abstract and intro only.
limits: The 39% is a best case. Per-dataset tables not extracted.
agent_relevance: Cheap graph expansion run by code, with no model in the walk, fits G5.

source: Jiang et al. (2026) SYNAPSE: episodic-semantic memory via spreading activation, arXiv 2601.02744
finding: Agent memory as a graph with spreading activation, lateral inhibition and temporal decay, fused with vector search. Targets contextual tunneling, where the root cause shares no wording with the query.
numbers: LoCoMo (GPT-4o-mini): average F1 40.5 (adversarial category excluded), +7.2 over A-Mem (33.3); Zep 39.7; AriGraph 33.7. Reported up to 23% better multi-hop accuracy and 95% fewer tokens than full context. Temporal edge decay 0.01.
limits: Authors' own runs; code promised on acceptance. Baselines may differ in settings.
agent_relevance: Closest published design to our S3 memory. Decay and inhibition live in code, not in the LLM.

source: Jiang et al. (2026) SYNAPSE ablation
finding: Removing the fan-effect term (damps hub nodes) caused a sharp drop, especially open-domain and multi-hop. Each mechanism had a targeted loss.
numbers: Open-Domain F1 fell from 25.9 to 16.8 without the fan effect (as read from text).
limits: One backbone; table not fully read.
agent_relevance: Hub damping (Anderson's fan effect) is needed or common entities swamp the walk.

source: Glybovets and Makarov (2026) Query-aware spreading activation for multi-hop retrieval, arXiv 2606.30133
finding: Each hop passes a gate set by cosine similarity between the candidate entity and the question. Fixed 3 iterations, run as one Neo4j query. The gate improved answers and sped retrieval.
numbers: MuSiQue EM 32.80 vs QAFD-RAG 33.50; beats HippoRAG by 5.3 EM and 3.4 F1. Gate ablation: F1 +3.6 to +7.4 points and latency cut 1.5 to 4.9 times.
limits: On 2WikiMultiHopQA HippoRAG and QAFD-RAG kept an advantage. One preprint, one embedding model and Gemini 2.5 Flash.
agent_relevance: Gate each hop by similarity to the question. Query-blind spread wastes budget on drift.

source: Anderson (1983) A spreading activation theory of memory, J Verbal Learn Verbal Behav 22:261-295
finding: ACT-style theory with node activation, link strengths and the fan effect: more links from a concept dilute activation to each. SYNAPSE cites it as a base for decay and fan-out.
numbers: Not read. The ACT-R site URL I tried returned nothing. Fan-effect RT values not verified.
limits: Cited via SYNAPSE and Hutchison (2003) only.
agent_relevance: The fan effect is the formal reason for hub damping in our graph retrieval.

source: Posner and Snyder (1975) Attention and cognitive control (Information processing and cognition)
finding: Defines automatic processing as quick, unintended spread that does not use limited capacity, versus slower strategic processing. Lucas (2000) cites an SOA over 250 ms as the point where strategy can act.
numbers: Not read. The 250 ms figure comes from Lucas (2000) text.
limits: Hutchison (2003) says no SOA cleanly splits the two.
agent_relevance: Keep a cheap automatic pass distinct from the deliberate pass.
